_why: ADR 0063 says the substrate publishes base images and the application composes base plus overlay. Nothing published them, and two CI comments said mind-pod-rails-base 'does not exist and never will' as a pullable name. This declares which images this substrate publishes, so a consumer has something to pin and a gate can hold the set both ways.

tagging.rule: immutable tag per commit: sha-<full 40-char commit SHA>
tagging.no_latest: A mutable tag is not a pin. This repo already refuses undigested FROM lines (check_base_digests.py); publishing a moving :latest and inviting consumers to build FROM it would give back what that gate buys.
tagging.consumer_guidance: Resolve the digest and pin that: docker buildx imagetools inspect ghcr.io/laquereric/magentic-stack/rails-base:sha-<SHA>

published.name: rails-base
published.because: The platform base. Its own header says consumers build a thin image FROM it. app-oriented-translation's Dockerfile.thin is exactly that consumer.

published.name: switch
published.because: The LLM plane. An application composing the pod runs it unchanged; it has no application-specific content.

published.name: mind
published.because: MIND. Needs the nooa submodule vendored before build, which is why an application cannot build it from a plain clone -- the strongest single reason to publish rather than have every consumer reproduce this.

not_published.because: The substrate's OWN Rails app (BACK and its roles). An application overlay builds its own thin layer FROM rails-base instead of consuming this one.
The CPCP FRONT accessory, paired to a specific BACK deployment. Not a substrate primitive.
Adapter wrapping the pinned upstream; built as part of switch, not shipped separately.

_scan_note: Directory names skipped when enumerating Dockerfiles. Held here as DATA, not as a literal in the checker. The trees they name are gitignored: present in a working clone, absent in a clean checkout. Enumerating them would give the gate two populations and a CI-only failure.
